subject.title: Durable Core PR 4/6: persist agent-turn front doors

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in durable core configuration and shared-state recovery contract across its Gateway, CLI, channel, cron, and HTTP front doors?
rationale: The branch is not a narrow repair: it creates a new persisted control plane, configuration modes, failure behavior, and recovery policy whose permanent core ownership cannot be established from tests alone.

options.title: Sponsor the durable core direction
options.body: Approve the core ownership and compatibility contract, then require the remaining real protocol proof before normal merge review.

options.title: Narrow to a foundation or owner-specific seam
options.body: Keep only a maintainer-approved minimal storage or owner-boundary change and move broad cross-front-door behavior into separately sponsored work.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Do not merge a new durable runtime contract until a maintainer-owned design and rollout plan exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the durable core direction
recommendation.body: Approve the core ownership and compatibility contract, then require the remaining real protocol proof before normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the connected durable PR3 recovery work and the proposed PR4 front-door implementation, so they can supply the technical contract details for maintainer sponsorship.
